edge_thesis: Friday AI-led equity rout pushed VIX to 35.89 and drove panic safe-haven flows into Treasuries and the yen, even as December Fed hike odds sit near 90% and Middle East shipping risks simmer. Sunday evening US equity futures (+2.1% S&P, +2.75% Nasdaq) and falling 10-year Treasury futures (+4bps yield) signal an unwinding of that panic safety bid into a thin Thanksgiving week with Tokyo closed Monday. On the other side are Friday forced de-leveragers, CTA/momentum yen and duration chasers who bought Treasuries at 5% yields into an impending Fed hike, and crowded tech/AI sellers rotating into lower-beta financials and cash-generative energy.

picks.why: Haven yen bid unwinds as US futures rebound, 10Y yields tick up, Tokyo closed for Labor Thanksgiving, and 275bp US-Japan carry favors USD.
Friday +1.37% equity-panic flight-to-safety pop reverses as Treasury futures drop Sunday night ahead of Wednesday PCE and 90%-priced Dec hike.
Oversold financials (14.4x fwd P/E, -7% last week) rebound on VIX 35.89 vol compression and higher yields without AI capex or SEC-probe headline risk.
Low-beta (0.20) relative-strength leader held green during Friday crash and captures Hormuz tanker-risk premium plus +8.6% European gas tailwinds.

self_disclosed_correlation: USDJPY long and TLT short share the same risk-on / higher-US-yields driver, so a sharp intraday equity selloff can snap both out simultaneously; XOM is the highest failure risk if risk-on fades oil.
